fields.name: Owner
fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x2E1FEA0 (size 0x20): three null handles at +0/+8/+0x10, word 0x16 at +0x18. esv::disarm::WeaponSystem update bg3.exe+0x2E1E150 creates it on a new entity for every entry of its request map (key = weapon, 0x18-byte value) and writes value[0] here. The Osiris event handler bg3.exe+0x30CF930 (registered by esv::StoryCharacterEventManager::Init) checks this handle as a character and sends it as the first argument.

fields.name: Weapon
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2E1E150 writes the map key here - the entity whose eoc::EquipableComponent slot is read and which is dropped as an item (esv::Item::GetItemTemplate). bg3.exe+0x30CF930 resolves it as an item and sends it as the second argument of the event.

fields.name: Disarmer
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2E1E150 writes value[1] of the request here. In the same function this entity, when alive and with a transform, gives the direction in which the weapon is thrown out (owner position minus its position, normalised) - the source of the disarm.

fields.name: Slot
fields.evidence: 1 byte. bg3.exe+0x2E1E150 writes the byte at +0x10 of the weapon's eoc::EquipableComponent (Slot), or 0x13 when the component is missing; default 0x16. bg3.exe+0x30CF930 passes it to eoc::equipment::EquipmentSlotToString for the third argument of the event.

fields.name: SkipDrop
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2E1E150 copies byte value[2] of the request here; in the same loop the whole branch that throws the weapon to the ground (direction, AI grid, drop movement) runs only when this byte is 0. Default 0.

fields.name: _Pad1A
fields.evidence: tail padding; the creator writes only a word at +0x18

open_questions: Who sets SkipDrop (value[2] of the request) was not traced; the name comes from the branch it disables.
second_pass: Every member offset and width is established on Windows (creator bg3.exe+0x2E1FEA0, writer esv::disarm::WeaponSystem bg3.exe+0x2E1E150, Osiris event handler bg3.exe+0x30CF930); not saved, no macOS FieldMeta, so names stay inferred.
